prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules induce proximity between a chosen protein and a cell's own E3 ubiquitin ligase so that it is destroyed, from the first PROTAC heterobifunctional degraders to the identification of cereblon as the target through which molecular-glue degraders act.

statement.case_for: After the first round I keep B052 first, and the exchange sharpened the reason. The discovery is one transferable principle: a small molecule induces proximity between an E3 ligase and a target, turning occupancy-driven pharmacology into catalytic, event-driven removal of the protein. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional version, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains why molecular glues degrade neomorphic substrates, so the two lineages are historically distinct but mechanistically one idea. The mechanism is validated by structures, independent reproduction in many laboratories and a large clinical pipeline, and it changed what chemists, chemical biologists and clinicians can do, which is the test I apply. Heiner's point that the citation must name the shared principle rather than tell two stories is right, and I have rewritten mine accordingly: induced proximity is the object, PROTACs and cereblon glues are the two demonstrations.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains lossy: Ciulli (rational VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures), Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito have real claims, and the three-person limit forces a cut that will look arbitrary to some. No PROTAC drug is approved, so the clinical proof of the PROTAC branch specifically is incomplete, although the approved-drug record for thalidomide analogues rests on the cereblon mechanism. Eight members produced six configurations, so B052 is not close to the five votes needed, and I must accept that a principle prize may lose to a more mature, cleanly attributed method.

responses.point: Cereblon explains glue degraders but is not the PROTAC concept, so the citation must name induced proximity to a ubiquitin ligase rather than list two stories, and the incomplete clinical record should not count heavily.
responses.response: I accept the first part and changed my citation: it now leads with the induced-proximity principle and names PROTACs and cereblon only as its two demonstrations. I do not accept dropping Handa, because without cereblon the glue strand has no molecular basis and the principle looks like a PROTAC-only story. On maturity I agree that the mechanism, not the pipeline, is what is being recognized, but I would not call the clinical record irrelevant. Heiner, what would you need to see in the committee text to be comfortable that Crews, Deshaies and Handa is one achievement and not a compromise?

responses.point: B052 rests on DC50 and Dmax readouts complicated by the hook effect, clinical proof for a PROTAC is pending, the trio may not treat Ciulli and Gray fairly, and the committee should settle that before ranking it first; B055 and B021 are paired instead.
responses.response: The measurement caveat is fair, but the hook effect is a consequence of the ternary-complex mechanism, and structures and kinetic work now explain it, so it argues for the principle rather than against it. On attribution I still hold Handa over Ciulli, because Ciulli's VHL ligands refined the PROTAC concept whereas cereblon opened a second lineage and explained an old drug, though with low confidence and I would discuss Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli if the committee wants a PROTAC-only citation. I do not see B055 plus B021 as stronger: it needs a two-part prize with Liu alone and leaves out Komor and Gaudelli, which is no cleaner than my cut.

responses.point: B052 is a comfortable fallback, but PROTAC (Crews, Deshaies) and cereblon glue (Handa, Ito) are close to two separate discoveries, Ciulli's structural work is decisive, and B055 has decades of validation.
responses.response: I agree B055 is the most mature case and that its chemistry is real, and your own comment that a molecular principle is stronger than an engineered platform is why I place B052 above it. Whether the strands are two discoveries is the real dispute; I read them as one design logic, induced proximity to an E3 ligase, found by two routes, and the revised citation says so. I take the structural point about Ciulli seriously and consider it the best argument for a different trio, but it does not outweigh the molecular-basis role of Handa.

responses.point: A PROTAC is a conjugation of known ligands so what is new is the concept rather than a new reaction, B052 is a strong second choice, and a fully mature, cleanly attributed method such as B031 should rank above it.
responses.response: I agree that chemically a PROTAC is not a new reaction; the novelty is the design principle, and I think the committee has rewarded concepts of that kind before. Where I differ is on B031: the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi and Migita precedents make it a method refinement within a recognized field, which for me weighs more than its maturity. I recognize your attribution is cleaner, and that is a genuine advantage over mine, but clean attribution does not outweigh a smaller conceptual step.

uncertainties: Whether Handa or Ciulli should hold the third seat, and whether a joint PROTAC and glue citation holds as one achievement.
How much weight the absence of an approved PROTAC drug should carry, given the cereblon-based approved drugs and late-stage degraders.
Whether the committee will converge on any candidate, since the first round gave six configurations, and whether the B052 supporters can reach five votes.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict or recusal is apparent. My postdoc mentors (Molly Stevens, Freddy Boey) and my Linkoping colleagues are not credited on any shortlisted ballot, and my self-assembly overlap with Emma Sparr is scientific, not a recusal matter. Nothing in round 1 changes this.
